title: Syno: Structured Synthesis for Neural Operators
problem: Neural architecture search (NAS) and tensor compilers both optimize over existing manually designed operators and cannot discover fundamentally new operator designs with better accuracy-performance tradeoffs. There is no systematic method to automatically synthesize novel neural operators that satisfy structural constraints required for trainability and hardware efficiency.
motivation: Manually designed neural operators are a fundamental bottleneck on both prediction accuracy and execution performance, and the space of possible operators is too large and complex to explore exhaustively by human intuition.
method: Syno defines a set of fine-grained primitives operating on tensor dimensions that enforce properties needed for stable model training (e.g., dimension matching, associativity). Expression canonicalization techniques prune redundant candidates during search. A guided synthesis flow constrains valid operators to specified input/output dimension sizes, and stochastic tree search (Monte Carlo-style) efficiently explores the large design space. The resulting operators are compiled and evaluated on real hardware.
key_novelty: End-to-end neural operator synthesis framework using fine-grained tensor-dimension primitives and stochastic tree search to automatically discover novel operators that outperform manually designed and NAS-optimized baselines.
contributions: Novel set of fine-grained tensor-dimension primitives that ensure trainability properties and enable expression canonicalization
Guided synthesis flow generating valid operators matched to specified input/output dimension constraints
Efficient stochastic tree search algorithm for exploring the neural operator design space
Discovered operators achieving 1.37x to 2.06x speedups on diverse hardware/compiler configurations with <1% accuracy loss even on NAS-optimized models

metrics.speedup: 1.37x to 2.06x average on various hardware and compiler choices

limitations: Not discussed; synthesis cost and scalability to very large models such as LLMs are not addressed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Automated neural operator synthesis via structured stochastic search
